verdicts.title: Complexity Results on DPLL and Resolution
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: DPLL and resolution are two popular methods for solving the problem of propositional satisfiability. Rather than algorithms, they are families of algorithms, as their behavior depend on some choices they face during execution: DPLL depends on the choice of the literal to branch on; resolution depends on the choice of the pair of clauses to resolve at each step. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses complexity-theoretic hardness of optimal branching/clause-choice and proof-size decisions in DPLL and resolution, not Hessian-rank or geometric obstructions bounding DPLL depth. It shares the DPLL vocabulary but does not interact with the specific Hessian-rank ≥ d_DPLL claim.

verdicts.title: Bi-polynomial rank and determinantal complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The permanent vs. determinant problem is one of the most important problems in theoretical computer science, and is the main target of geometric complexity theory proposed by Mulmuley and Sohoni. The current best lower bound for the determinantal complexity of the d by d permanent polynomial is d^2/2, due to Mignon and Ressayre in 2004. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns bi-polynomial rank lower bounds for determinantal complexity in the permanent vs. determinant problem, with no mention of DPLL search depth, 3-CNF formulas, or tree-resolution; it shares only the GCT/Mignon-Ressayre framework but does not interact with the specific Hessian-rank vs. DPLL-depth claim.

verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity ('deterministic communication complexity... equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix'), which shares the vocabulary of 'rank' but does not address Hessian rank of clause-count polynomials or DPLL search-tree depth.
